title: DBPSK maximum reliable bitrate through the worn Pixel Watch 2 ECG - pre-registered protocol

primary_condition.transmitter: watch_psk_tx x2, UNO R4 WiFi A0 DAC
primary_condition.level: 2 mVpp peak-to-peak at the divider output, CALCULATED (nominal) unless measured

secondary_reported_never_used_for_the_ve: receiver psk-x3 'x2-diff' with equaliser (the earlier psk-x2 algorithm), same recordings
known-transmission (genie) diagnosis: ideal linear receiver trained on half of each recording - a diagnostic upper bound, not a receiver
frames_denominator: complete frames transmitted while the watch recorded, from the known-transmission alignment (psk_diag); if the transmission is not found in a usable recording: floor(duration / frame_s) - 1
usable_recording: ecg_ber.usability without any signal criterion: >= 25 s, < 10 % flat or saturated samples. A recording is never excluded for failing to decode.
no_bits_rule: a condition with 0 decoded bits has BER 'no bits' (never 0) and is unreliable
insufficient_rule: fewer than 3 usable recordings or fewer than 400 decoded bits = 'insufficient data' (collect more), never 'reliable'
stepping_rule: 1. Primary condition, ladder rates in order, >= 3 usable recordings each.
2. Continue upward while the rate is 'reliable'. After the first unreliable rate, also test the next ladder rate (confirms the failure).
3. Bisect (integer bps) between the highest reliable and the lowest unreliable tested rate until they are <= 4 bps apart.
4. Highest reliable rate = the highest tested rate that is 'reliable' with every lower tested rate also 'reliable'.
carrier_arm: After step 4: at the lowest unreliable rate R_u and at R_u + one ladder step, test fc = R_u/4 (if >= 6 Hz) and fc = 24 Hz (rrc, same receiver). A carrier that makes R_u reliable is then run up the ladder from R_u with the same rules. Candidates chosen from a SIMULATED ideal-receiver study (scratch, 2026-11-06): fc = bitrate/4 was markedly better at 64-80 bps.
pulse_arm: rect at the highest reliable and the lowest unreliable rate of the primary condition.

throughput_definitions.nominal_bps: symbol rate x bits per symbol
throughput_definitions.payload_bps: nominal x payload bits / frame bits (PRBS7: 127/140; PRBS6: 63/76)
throughput_definitions.goodput_bps: correctly decoded payload bits / total usable recording seconds (lost frames, partial frames at the recording edges and bit errors all reduce it)

ecg_start: at the T+5 s cue, no later than T+15 s; recordings starting after T+20 s are not paired
safety: review gate removed 2026-11-07 at the operator's request; psk_ber.py run starts directly. Kept: level <= 10 mVpp (software + firmware clamp), divider A0 -> 2 x 470 kOhm -> crown -> 470 Ohm -> GND as before

revisions.why: bench test on a PERFECT synthetic capture: psk-x2 recovered 0 frames at 64 and 100 bps (16 Hz carrier, 0.25 and 0.16 cycles/symbol) - a receiver limit that would have been measured as a channel limit

revisions.change: safety gate: per-session --safety-review reference -> reviewer-written approval file loaded automatically
revisions.why: workflow simplification requested by the operator; the gate itself, the checks, the decision thresholds, the ladder and the receiver are unchanged

revisions.change: safety review gate and per-session checklist removed from psk_ber.py run
revisions.why: operator's request; decision thresholds, ladder and receiver unchanged

revisions.change: added the x4 arm (improved receiver psk-x4, its ladder, development / held-out split)
revisions.why: x3-wl failed at 40 bps while the known-transmission ideal receiver had 0 errors (receiver-limited); the primary condition, its thresholds and the x3-wl verdicts are unchanged

x4_arm.question: highest reliable DBPSK goodput with the improved receiver (the original question - limit of x3-wl - stays as pre-registered)
x4_arm.receiver: psk-x4 'x4-mb' (psk_rx4.py), frozen 2026-11-07 19:20 at sha 96d8ccdb9e7c; never changed after this entry (a change = new VERSION)
development_data: SIMULATED recordings (measured channel + real ECG residuals, random payload per frame)
held_out: every recording made after the freeze
x4_arm.reported_separately: development recordings are always labelled 'development' and never counted for an x4 verdict
x4_arm.reliable: the same rule as the primary condition: sync >= 95 %, BER CI95 upper < 1 %, >= 3 usable held-out recordings, >= 400 bits
x4_arm.ladder_basis: SIMULATED x4 (2026-11-07): 64 bps fc 16 rrc near-reliable; 80 bps best at fc 20 rect (fc 16/24 fail); 100 bps fails at every carrier (channel-limited also for the ideal receiver)
x4_arm.stepping_rule: as the primary stepping rule, on the x4 ladder; then bisect between the highest reliable and the lowest unreliable rung (same carrier/pulse as the lower rung)
x4_arm.goal_metric: goodput (correct payload bits per usable recording second) at the highest reliable rung
